body:
15 Nov 2026, READ-ONLY CHECKS ON VM 108 for the N-34 design (the advisor asked for them before any design).
(1) Do the album-less refs already know the catalogue? NO. Of the 673 refs with no album (595 hold the literal '[Unknown Album]', 78 are NULL), 650 have a kept YouTube file and NONE has a deezer_id. 'Requiem' (sr_01M6TYJHN8XAJEH42X5TWQ7FRW): deezer_id NULL, cover_tried_at NULL; 'Creature' (sr_01M6TYJHP7ECPPFXK065S0ACZ7): deezer_id NULL, cover_tried_at 7 Nov. So the album is NOT one cached lookup away: the catalogue has never been asked about these songs by title and artist (the cover finder stores a cover, not an identity). A repair is one gated Deezer search per song (about 650 on VM 108; the gate allows 20 requests in 5 s, so minutes, once), resumable, with a remembered miss.
(2) Does a NEW ref still get the literal? NO. The literal rows were all created 6 and 7 Nov (before the N-11 guard of 14 Nov 03:00 UTC); 0 refs created after it carry it, new album-less refs are NULL (78 of them, created up to 15 Nov). refs.py's update path skips the placeholder (is_placeholder_album) and the new refs are clean: no small bug to fix separately. The 595 old literals are harmless to the display (album_names.dart) but are data to normalise to NULL in the same repair.
(3) What decides the design: the repair of kept files moves them (Singles -> album folder), re-tags them and needs a scan; a moved file is a NEW music-server song id (N-26 slice 5 has the same step): so N-34 and N-26 slice 5 are ONE repair, and it needs an advisor ruling as a design-only PR (like #74 N-26 and #75 P2-12) BEFORE any code: where the identity lookup lives (cover_finder's catalogue step, store deezer_id + album + track_no + year on the ref), how a wrong album is avoided (match by title, artist AND duration; a live or cover version must not get a studio album), what happens to the 2nd Creature ref (a pair, B-110 family), whether the keeper's new keeps (not only the repair) do the lookup before the file is placed, and the undo (the old path is logged per file).
